reader.decision: Hand Petra the corrected version: the cache key gets the negotiated format (avif, webp or orig) from negotiate, not the whole Accept header. Petra then changes cache_key in edge/cache.py.
reader.decision_reason: The message corrects my understanding: the key appends negotiate's output, not the full Accept header, which would fragment the cache. The Safari 13 cause is confirmed, so the earlier ruling stands and the work can go to Petra.

reconstruction.problem: img-edge caches images under the URL only (path plus query string). A WebP variant cached after a Chrome request is served to Safari 13, which cannot decode WebP or AVIF.
reconstruction.what_breaks: Safari 13 users see broken product images when a WebP entry is already cached under the shared key.
reconstruction.fix: Change cache_key in edge/cache.py to append the output of negotiate(request.headers.get('Accept', '')), which is avif, webp or orig. The key becomes {path}?{query_string}#{format}. The key must not include the whole Accept header.
reconstruction.cost: Up to 3 cache entries per image instead of 1. Using the whole Accept header would have cost up to 1,912 entries per image (the distinct values seen in October) and a lower hit rate. The message gives no other cost.

reader.closing_answer: Not quite. The first and third points are right: today the key is the URL only, and the images break because Safari 13 cannot decode WebP. The second is wrong. The key gets the negotiated format (avif, webp or orig), not the whole Accept header. I hand Petra that corrected version.
